findings.title: Pausing a city, or deleting a pincode from its coverage, does not stop serviceability or fulfilment — the fulfilment path never reads city_launch_configs
findings.reproduction: cd /tmp/mc && node --experimental-strip-types REPRO.mjs  (block F1). Steps: seed city_launch_configs; POST /api/city-governance {action:"save_city", city:{id:"bengaluru", status:"Paused", pincodes: <seeded list with 560034 removed>, ...}} as a launch.manage actor; then (a) call resolveCityServiceCoverage(db,{cityCode:"blr",serviceCode:"grooming",pincode:"560034"}), (b) GET /api/service-zone?pincode=560034, (c) POST /api/grooming-service-location {bookingId:"BK1",customerId:"CUST1",address:"221B Koramangala 5th Block",pincode:"560034"} against a canonical_bookings row with city_id='blr', zone_id='blr-south', service_code='grooming'.
findings.expected: Once a city is Paused (or a pincode is removed from its coverage) in the only launch-governance surface the product has, the customer serviceability lookup and the doorstep-address gate must both refuse. The correct refusal semantics for Paused vs Draft vs Pilot is a product decision — but 'the pause control has literally no effect on any customer or fulfilment path' cannot be the intended one.
findings.consequence: The City & Geofence console is the founder's only kill switch for a market. Pausing Bengaluru — because a monsoon, a licensing problem, a provider walkout, or a safety incident closed the market — leaves the customer app resolving zones normally, and lets a customer save an active doorstep service address plus a default address record for a booking, generating a navigation URL for a provider to drive to. The operator believes the city is closed; the system keeps taking work in it. resolveZoneByPincode (the actual gate) never queries city_launch_configs at all, and radius_km/centre are read by nothing outside city-governance.ts.
findings.rule_source: NONE -> decision ledger. app/control/city-control-panel.tsx line 104 states to the operator: "Customer address must fall inside the active radius or approved pincodes." and line 87 renders a "Live geofences / Radius/pincode rules" tile. No rule anywhere defines what Paused must do to in-flight serviceability. The question for the ledger: when a city is Paused or a pincode is de-advertised, which of {new quotes, new bookings, address capture on existing bookings, in-flight fulfilment} must stop, and immediately or at the next booking boundary?
findings.suggested_fix: Make city_launch_configs the authority the fulfilment path consults: have resolveZoneByPincode (or a wrapper the routes call) join the resolved cityId to city_launch_configs and refuse unless status is Live (or Pilot, per the ledger decision), and intersect the resolved pincode with that city's advertised coverage. Until that exists, the panel copy claiming address/radius/pincode enforcement should be removed rather than left as a false statement to the operator.

findings.title: A second city can be published Live with priced services while no pincode in it is bookable, and no API exists to make one bookable
findings.reproduction: cd /tmp/mc && node --experimental-strip-types REPRO.mjs  (block F2). POST /api/city-governance {action:"save_city", city:{cityCode:"mum", city:"Mumbai", state:"Maharashtra", status:"Live", centre:"19.0760, 72.8777", radiusKm:30, pincodes:"400001,400050,400070", gstIncluded:true, services:{all four enabled with prices}}}; then GET /api/service-zone?pincode=<each>, GET /api/service-zone?action=list, and POST /api/service-zone with any mapping-style action.
findings.expected: Either saving a city as Live must require that its coverage is actually resolvable (refuse the transition to Live with 409 and name the unmapped pincodes), or the platform must expose an authenticated way to register pincode -> zone mappings for a new city. Publishing Live with zero fulfilable coverage and no remedy short of a code deploy is not a coherent launch path.
findings.consequence: 'Launch a city' is a dead end. The founder marks Mumbai Live, sets four service prices, saves 201, and the City Directory shows it Live — while every Mumbai customer who enters a PIN code is told they are outside the service area, and the zone catalogue the mobile address picker renders lists only the five Bengaluru zones. The panel additionally promises 'Publish protection: Draft -> validate coverage & prices -> owner approval -> city goes live'; the measured path is one POST straight to Live with no coverage validation and no approval step. The only writer to service_zone_mappings anywhere in the codebase is seedDefaultZones, which is hardcoded to the 72 Bengaluru pincodes with city_id='blr' — so a second city is reachable only via a code change to PINCODE_ZONE_MAP or by hand-writing D1 rows in production.
findings.rule_source: NONE -> decision ledger. app/control/city-control-panel.tsx line 83 ("Launch a city with its own coverage and prices") and line 107 ("Draft -> validate coverage & prices -> owner approval -> city goes live") describe a launch workflow that does not exist. Question for the ledger: what evidence must a city present before status Live is permitted — at minimum, N resolvable pincode->zone mappings and >=1 governed provider whose profile city_id matches?
findings.suggested_fix: Add an authenticated action to /api/service-zone that upserts a pincode->zone->city mapping (settings.manage, audited), and gate the Draft->Live transition in city-governance validate() on every advertised pincode resolving through resolveZoneByPincode. Make listServiceZones union the DB-registered zones so the catalogue surface matches the resolver.

findings.title: Concurrent city-coverage saves race: an operator's audit row records the OTHER operator's coverage as what they saved, and both rows claim the same version
findings.reproduction: cd /tmp/mc && node --experimental-strip-types REPRO.mjs  (block F3). await Promise.all([ saveCityLaunchConfig(db,{id:"bengaluru",...,pincodes:"560034,560102"},"ops-A@pawspace.in"), saveCityLaunchConfig(db,{id:"bengaluru",...,pincodes:"560001,560002"},"ops-B@pawspace.in") ]) against the seeded bengaluru row (version 1), then read city_launch_configs and city_launch_config_audit directly.
findings.expected: One of the two saves must fail (409 stale version) or the two must serialize into versions 2 and 3. An audit row attributed to ops-A must contain the coverage ops-A actually submitted; two audit rows for the same config must never carry the same version number; and the 201 body returned to ops-A must describe ops-A's own write.
findings.consequence: Coverage is the record of which pincodes the business promises to serve, and city_launch_config_audit is the only trail of who changed it. After the race, that trail is not merely lossy — it is false: it asserts that ops-A set coverage to 560001,560002, which ops-A never submitted. ops-A's own 201 response also shows 560001,560002 and updatedBy ops-B, so ops-A sees a success screen for a change that was silently discarded and walks away believing 560034 and 560102 are live. Both audit rows carry version 2, so version can no longer order the history. The cause is a read-decide-write with no guard: `version = before.version+1` is computed from a SELECT (line 86/91), and after the INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE the function re-SELECTs the row (line 94) to build both the audit payload and the response — by then the other writer's row has landed.
findings.rule_source: Repository invariant: city_launch_configs carries a `version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1` column and every save writes a before/after audit pair (lib/city-governance.ts lines 91, 97-98), i.e. the schema asserts an ordered, attributable change history. The race violates that assertion.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the write conditional on the version read: `... ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET ... WHERE city_launch_configs.version = ?` bound to before.version, check meta.changes, and return 409 with the current version when it is 0. Build the audit after_json and the response body from the values actually written rather than from a re-SELECT.

findings.title: resolveCityServiceCoverage returns supported:true with reason "live_and_explicitly_supported" when no usable pincode was supplied, and for a Live city whose coverage list is empty
findings.reproduction: cd /tmp/mc && node --experimental-strip-types REPRO.mjs  (block F4). seedDefaultCityLaunchConfigs, then call resolveCityServiceCoverage(db,{cityCode:"blr",serviceCode:"grooming"}) with pincode absent / null / "" / "abc" / "5600341". Then POST /api/city-governance save_city for a Live centre-only city (pincodes:"") and query it with and without a pincode.
findings.expected: An unknown location is not a supported location. With no usable pincode the answer must be a distinct third state (e.g. supported:false / reason:"pincode_required", or supported:"unknown"), never supported:true — and certainly never carrying the literal claim "live_and_explicitly_supported", which asserts a check that was skipped. A Live city whose only declared coverage rule is a radius must not answer "explicitly supported" for a caller who gave no coordinates either.
findings.consequence: This is the house defect in its purest form: `const pincode=String(input.pincode||"").replace(/\D/g,"").slice(0,6); if(pincode){...}` (lines 50-54) — an absent, empty or non-numeric pincode falls out of the guard entirely and the function returns supported:true with a startingPrice. Any caller that asks the coverage question before the customer has typed a PIN code (a landing page, a chat bot, a phone agent, a price widget) is told the service is explicitly supported there and given a price to quote. The Hyderabad case is worse: validate() explicitly permits a Live city with centre+radius and no pincodes (line 65, "Add centre coordinates or serviceable pincodes"), the radius is then never applied by anything, so the city's ONLY coverage rule is unenforceable and the pincode-less query reports it as explicitly supported at Rs 1499. HONEST SCOPE: no production route calls resolveCityServiceCoverage today — it is reached only from tests/uat-closure-cross-module-governance.test.mjs, which is the suite that certifies coverage. So the live blast radius is the certification, not a customer screen, until the first route wires it up.
findings.rule_source: lib/pincode-validation.ts lines 5-10 state the house rule for this boundary: "Keep this strict: do not strip letters/punctuation or truncate longer input, because doing so can silently turn garbage into a different, serviceable PIN." resolveCityServiceCoverage does exactly the stripping and truncating that comment forbids, and then treats the resulting empty string as 'no constraint' rather than 'no answer'.
findings.suggested_fix: Run the input through validateIndianPincode and branch on all three outcomes: ok -> check the advertised set; missing -> return a distinct {supported:false, reason:"pincode_required"}; malformed -> {supported:false, reason:"invalid_pincode"}. Separately, refuse Live for a city whose advertised coverage contains no valid pincode until the radius rule is actually implemented and applied.

findings.title: zone.serviceAvailable is a hardcoded true on every producible path — every "is this zone open?" gate downstream is dead, and there is no way to close a zone
findings.reproduction: cd /tmp/mc && node --experimental-strip-types REPRO.mjs  (block F5). resolveZoneByPincode for an in-memory pincode (560034), for a DB-only second-city pincode (400050 inserted as mum-west/mum/Mumbai/Bandra West), and listServiceZones. Then attempt to close a zone: there is no writer for serviceAvailable anywhere — the DB-fallback branch synthesizes it as a literal true (line 137) and SERVICE_ZONES declares it true for all five zones (lines 101-105); service_zone_mappings has no availability column at all (line 110 DDL).
findings.expected: Either serviceAvailable is backed by state an operator can change (a column on service_zone_mappings, or a zone registry table), or the four downstream consumers that branch on it should not pretend to.
findings.consequence: Four separate gates read this flag and none of them can ever fire: app/api/grooming-service-location/route.ts line 29 refuses with 409 "The service address is outside an enabled PawSpace zone" when !serviceAvailable; lib/training-booking-guards.ts line 38 refuses with "<zone> is not open for Dog Training yet"; lib/service-zone-client.ts line 30 throws "PIN code X is outside the currently enabled service area"; app/mobile-app/address-picker.tsx line 103 renders a "✓ Available" / "Not available" badge that can only ever render "✓ Available". The product therefore has no lever at all to close a single zone — not for a provider shortage, a flooded area, a safety incident, or a service not yet launched in that zone. Worse, the synthesized branch for a DB-registered second-city zone hardcodes serviceAvailable:true (line 137), so any zone row an operator adds is born open with no way to open or close it deliberately. The tests already exercise the false branch synthetically (tests/training-booking-guards.test.mjs line 100 passes serviceAvailable:false by hand), which is why the dead gate has never been noticed.
findings.rule_source: Repository invariant / self-contradiction: the ServiceZone type declares serviceAvailable as a per-zone boolean and four call sites branch on it, i.e. the code asserts it is variable state. Execution shows it is a constant. No product rule is needed to see the contradiction.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a service_available column to service_zone_mappings (or a service_zone_registry table) plus an authenticated action to toggle it, and have resolveZoneByPincode read it for both branches instead of returning a literal. If per-zone closure is not wanted, delete the field and the four dead branches so no surface claims a state that cannot occur.

findings.title: POST /api/service-zone {action:"seed"} reports "Default zones seeded" but leaves a wrong zone_id and area untouched — the remediation endpoint claims a repair it did not perform
findings.reproduction: cd /tmp/mc && node --experimental-strip-types REPRO.mjs  (block F6). Insert the exact fabricated rows the code comment (lib/service-zones.ts lines 9-13) says originally shipped — 560048 -> blr-north / "Whitehall", 560018 -> blr-west / "Koramangala" — then POST /api/service-zone {action:"seed"} as a settings.manage actor with a same-origin header, and re-read the rows.
findings.expected: A seed action that answers 200 "Default zones seeded" must leave service_zone_mappings equal to the reviewed PINCODE_ZONE_MAP — 560048 must become blr-east / "Hoodi & ITPL" and 560018's area must become "Chamarajpet" — or it must report that it declined to overwrite operator-modified rows and name them.
findings.consequence: The ON CONFLICT clause is `DO UPDATE SET city_id=COALESCE(service_zone_mappings.city_id,'blr')` (line 158): it backfills city_id and nothing else, so zone_id, city and area of an existing row are never corrected. The exact fabricated data the module's own comment identifies as the original production defect — Whitefield filed under blr-north, "Whitehall" as a locality, Koramangala's name attached to 560018 (which is Chamarajpet) — survives the repair endpoint, and the endpoint answers 200 with a success message. Ops runs the fix, sees success, and stops looking. Today those 72 pincodes are shadowed by the in-memory map so bookings are unaffected, but service_zone_mappings is the table an operator queries for coverage reporting and is the sole authority for any pincode NOT in the hardcoded map — so the stale rows are both a reporting lie now and a live wrong answer the moment a pincode is moved out of the code map, which is the stated migration direction (lines 132-135: "A database row is an explicit, operations-reviewed mapping. It must be usable for a launched second city without requiring a code deployment").
findings.rule_source: Repository invariant: the function is named seedDefaultZones and the route answers "Default zones seeded"; both assert post-condition equality with PINCODE_ZONE_MAP. Execution shows the post-condition does not hold.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the conflict clause to the identity columns the seed owns — `DO UPDATE SET zone_id=excluded.zone_id, city=excluded.city, area=excluded.area, city_id=COALESCE(service_zone_mappings.city_id,'blr')` — or, if operator edits must be preserved, detect divergent rows and return them in the response instead of a bare success message.

findings.title: City coverage is unvalidated free text: named clusters are silently dropped and a 7-digit typo is truncated into a different, real, serviceable pincode
findings.reproduction: cd /tmp/mc && node --experimental-strip-types REPRO.mjs  (block F7). POST /api/city-governance save_city with pincodes set to the control panel's own placeholder string "600001, 600002, OMR, Anna Nagar"; then query coverage for 600001 and 600020. Then save a city with pincodes:"5600341" and query it with "560034". Also resolveZoneByPincode(db,"5600341") and validateIndianPincode("5600341") for contrast.
findings.expected: validate() must parse the coverage field and reject or explicitly report every token that is not a valid Indian PIN code, and normalisation must not truncate: an over-length token is malformed, not a prefix. validateIndianPincode already implements exactly this policy and returns {ok:false,reason:"malformed"} for "5600341" — the two coverage resolvers do not use it.
findings.consequence: Two distinct wrong outcomes from one unvalidated field. (1) Silent narrowing: the panel's own placeholder text invites "600001, 600002, OMR, Anna Nagar", and "OMR" and "Anna Nagar" — two of the largest residential corridors in Chennai — are dropped without a word; the operator believes four coverage entries are live and two are void. "not a pincode at all" saves 201 onto a Live city. (2) Silent widening into the wrong place: a fat-fingered "5600341" becomes 560034 — a real, live, Koramangala pincode — in BOTH directions (advertised as coverage, and accepted as a customer query). resolveZoneByPincode does the same truncation. This is precisely the failure lib/pincode-validation.ts was written to prevent, and its doc comment names it. HONEST SCOPE: /api/service-zone GET does gate on validateIndianPincode and returns 400 for "5600341", and /api/grooming-service-location rejects 7 digits with its own /^\d{6}$/ test, so the truncation in resolveZoneByPincode is currently unreachable from those two routes; the truncation in resolveCityServiceCoverage and in the stored coverage field is reachable today by any operator save.
findings.rule_source: lib/pincode-validation.ts lines 5-10 (the repository's own stated rule for this boundary): "Keep this strict: do not strip letters/punctuation or truncate longer input, because doing so can silently turn garbage into a different, serviceable PIN."
findings.suggested_fix: In validate(), split the coverage field, run each token through validateIndianPincode, and reject the save naming every rejected token (or persist a normalised, parsed list plus a separate cluster-names field if named clusters are a real product need). In resolveCityServiceCoverage and resolveZoneByPincode, replace `.replace(/\D/g,"").slice(0,6)` with validateIndianPincode and fail closed on malformed.

findings.title: A service-zone row carries two independent city identities and nothing cross-checks them: a Bengaluru zone id on a Mumbai pincode returns "East Bengaluru" to a Bandra customer
findings.reproduction: cd /tmp/mc && node --experimental-strip-types REPRO.mjs  (block F8). INSERT INTO service_zone_mappings (pincode,zone_id,city_id,city,area,created_at) VALUES ('400050','blr-east','mum','Mumbai','Bandra West',1); then resolveZoneByPincode(db,"400050").
findings.measured_before: {"zone":{"zoneId":"blr-east","zoneName":"East Bengaluru","description":"Indiranagar, Whitefield, Marathahalli, Bellandur","color":"#00BCD4","serviceAvailable":true},"assignment":{"pincode":"400050","zoneId":"blr-east","cityId":"mum","city":"Mumbai","area":"Bandra West"}}
findings.expected: The row's city_id and the zone's owning city must be reconciled. Either the lookup refuses when the resolved zone belongs to a different city than the row's city_id (the module's own stated posture — line 135, "an incomplete row cannot silently open a service area"), or SERVICE_ZONES is keyed by city so a cross-city zone id cannot be matched at all.
findings.consequence: resolveZoneByPincode gives the DB row's city_id ('mum') to the assignment while taking the zone presentation from the Bengaluru-only SERVICE_ZONES constant, because it looks the zone id up in a global map with no city scoping (line 137). A Bandra West customer is shown "East Bengaluru — Indiranagar, Whitefield, Marathahalli, Bellandur" as their service zone in the address picker, and that zone id is then carried forward as the booking's zone_id and matched against provider zones_json and scheduling_availability rows keyed to Bengaluru operations. The module explicitly claims to fail closed on incomplete identity but does not check identity consistency — all four fields being non-empty is treated as sufficient. findings.title: IDfy callback deduplication keys on event id alone, so a redelivery carrying a DIFFERENT outcome is answered 200 accepted with the OLD outcome and silently discarded
findings.reproduction:
/tmp/kyc/p8.mjs steps 1 and 2, with a real HMAC over `${stamp}.${rawBody}` via idfyHmacHex and a stubbed submission transport (our contract only - no real IDfy account exists here):
  send({event_id:'EV1',request_id:'IDFY-REQ-001',status:'completed',result:{verification_status:'verified'}})
  send({event_id:'EV1',request_id:'IDFY-REQ-001',status:'completed',result:{verification_status:'not_verified'}})
Line 112 selects on provider_event_id alone; payload_sha256 is computed at line 104 and stored at line 121 but never compared.

-- 1. verified callback --
{"accepted":true,"status":200,"applicationId":"POAPP-TEST-1","verificationType":"aadhaar","outcome":"verified","duplicate":false}
row: [ { verification_type: 'aadhaar', status: 'verified', updated_by: 'idfy_callback' } ]
-- 2. SAME event_id, DIFFERENT payload saying failed --
{"accepted":true,"status":200,"applicationId":"POAPP-TEST-1","verificationType":"aadhaar","outcome":"verified","duplicate":true}
row: [ { verification_type: 'aadhaar', status: 'verified' } ]
callback rows: [ { provider_event_id: 'EV1', outcome: 'verified', accepted: 1, payload_sha256: 'e682238998014d342625fab781f0c461d7abe05b000e7cc5fa476f02f803e352' } ]
findings.expected: The replay key must bind the payload, not just the event id. A delivery whose payload_sha256 differs from the stored one is not a redelivery - it should either be applied (subject to the existing monotonic rule) or refused loudly, but it must never be answered accepted:true with a stale outcome that the caller then reports as the truth.
findings.consequence: A revocation delivered under a reused or colliding event id is dropped, IDfy is told 200 (stop retrying), and the returned body asserts the old 'verified' outcome to whatever called the route. A provider whose Aadhaar was revoked stays verified and assignment-eligible with no trace anywhere except a payload hash nobody compares. The rest of this boundary is well built (503 on absent secret, absolute-difference freshness window, constant-time compare, terminal-state monotonicity - all verified in the same run); this is the one hole left.
findings.rule_source: lib/idfy-callback-boundary.ts:17-19 and 106-113, which state the dedup contract as 'a redelivery ... answers 200 and changes no state' - a delivery with different content is not a redelivery, and the code already stores the hash that would tell the two apart.
findings.suggested_fix: Include payload_sha256 in the replay lookup at line 112 (or compare it after the match) and treat a same-event-id/different-hash delivery as a fresh callback routed through the normal correlation and monotonic-update path.
